pages.quiz:
AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #13
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. After about how long should the compost heap first be turned? (1 mark)
   A. Never
   B. One year
   C. One hour
   D. Two to three weeks

2. How can compost be used in a garden? (1 mark)
   A. Throw it away
   B. Use it to build a wall
   C. Feed it to fish
   D. Mix it in planting holes or spread it around crops

3. Where is the neck of the bottle placed in a bottle drip system? (1 mark)
   A. High in a tree
   B. On the leaves
   C. In the soil beside the plant
   D. In the bucket

4. What does mulch do? (1 mark)
   A. Makes the soil hot
   B. Keeps the soil moist by reducing evaporation
   C. Kills the plant
   D. Adds plastic to the soil

5. Which statement about a three-stone fire is correct? (1 mark)
   A. It never needs firewood
   B. It loses a lot of heat to the air
   C. It saves the most fuel
   D. It is completely smoke-free

6. Why should you prepare all the food before lighting the fire? (1 mark)
   A. To use more wood
   B. To cook faster than a cooker
   C. To make the food colder
   D. So the fire does not burn while you are still preparing

7. What might a hungry hare eat in a garden? (1 mark)
   A. Glass
   B. Stones
   C. Metal
   D. Young shoots of vegetables

8. Why are tins with pebbles tied on a scarecrow? (1 mark)
   A. They feed birds
   B. They store water
   C. They make noise and flash to frighten animals
   D. They make it heavy

9. What should be done first before pulling out seedlings when thinning? (1 mark)
   A. Cover it with plastic
   B. Cut the tops off
   C. Water the bed so the soil is soft
   D. Dry the bed

10. What is a grafted seedling? (1 mark)
   A. A seed in a bag
   B. A young tree joined with a branch from a good tree
   C. A plant grown in water
   D. A dead plant

11. How should the seedling be removed from its polythene bag? (1 mark)
   A. By cutting the roots
   B. Carefully so the ball of soil around roots does not break
   C. By pulling the stem hard
   D. By throwing it

12. What should be done with extra fruits? (1 mark)
   A. Leave them to rot
   B. Share or sell them and avoid wasting
   C. Bury them
   D. Throw them away

13. Which is a way of protecting ripe fruit from birds and monkeys? (1 mark)
   A. Poison the animals
   B. Cover trees with nets or use scare methods
   C. Leave them ripe for months
   D. Cut the tree

14. Why should hands be washed after handling chickens? (1 mark)
   A. To colour the hands
   B. To warm the hands
   C. To remove germs
   D. To get feathers off

15. Which of these fruits is a protective food? (1 mark)
   A. Rice
   B. Butter
   C. Chapati
   D. Orange

16. Which activity is part of keeping a food journal? (1 mark)
   A. Cooking only
   B. Buying food
   C. Throwing food away
   D. Writing what you eat at each meal

17. Which fruit is a protective food? (1 mark)
   A. Rice
   B. Ugali
   C. Mango
   D. Chapati

18. Which of these belongs to more than one group? (1 mark)
   A. Salt
   B. Water
   C. Sugar
   D. Groundnuts

19. What is one way to choose foods for a balanced meal? (1 mark)
   A. Pick only cheap food
   B. Pick only your favourite food
   C. Pick one or more foods from each group
   D. Pick only sweet food

20. Why are eggs put in cold water after boiling? (1 mark)
   A. To colour them
   B. To make them raw again
   C. To cool them so they are easy to peel
   D. To make them larger

21. What is cooking? (1 mark)
   A. Washing food
   B. Storing food
   C. Cutting food
   D. Preparing food using heat

22. What is refuse? (1 mark)
   A. Food
   B. Clean water
   C. Rubbish or waste
   D. Soap

23. Why should the compound be free of long grass and rubbish? (1 mark)
   A. Snakes, rats and mosquitoes can hide there
   B. To save soap
   C. To stop rain
   D. It looks colourful

24. Why should torn gloves not be used? (1 mark)
   A. They are too big
   B. They are too clean
   C. They may not protect the hands
   D. They are too heavy

25. Why is a display of clean PPE useful? (1 mark)
   A. It wastes time
   B. It makes PPE dirty
   C. It helps others learn about PPE and hygiene
   D. It hides the PPE

26. Which skill from Mathematics helps in tacking? (1 mark)
   A. Telling time
   B. Measuring
   C. Adding money
   D. Naming shapes only

27. Which thread colour is best for tacking? (1 mark)
   A. One that shows clearly on the cloth
   B. White on white
   C. Black on black
   D. One matching the cloth exactly

28. About how long is the long stitch in long and short tacking? (1 mark)
   A. 2 mm
   B. 2 cm
   C. 20 cm
   D. 2 metres

29. Which of these is another tacking stitch? (1 mark)
   A. Blanket stitch
   B. Herringbone
   C. Long and short tacking
   D. French knot

30. How much of each edge is folded twice for the handkerchief hem? (1 mark)
   A. 10 cm
   B. 20 cm
   C. 1 mm
   D. About 1 cm each time

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Explain how to look after a compost heap for two months. (4 marks)

32. Explain four things that may happen to a child who does not eat a balanced diet. (4 marks)

33. Write the steps for growing carrots from seed to harvest. (5 marks)

34. How can you tell that compost is ready for use? (3 marks)

35. Name two types of tacking stitches and describe each. (3 marks)

36. Describe how a family can plant trees to help conserve fuel. (4 marks)

37. Name the young of a cow, a goat and a sheep. (3 marks)

38. Name three improvised cleaning tools and what each is made from. (3 marks)

39. Why should personal items like towels not be shared? (2 marks)

40. Compare even tacking and long and short tacking. Say which is quicker and which holds more firmly. (4 marks)

41. Why do some fruit trees take longer to give fruit than others? (3 marks)

42. List three things needed to make a bucket drip system. (3 marks)

43. Give three reasons why PPE should be cleaned. (3 marks)

44. Explain four benefits of conserving fuel. (4 marks)

45. How can a family get a balanced meal cheaply? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #13 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — Two to three weeks
   Turning after a few weeks gives air and mixes the heap.

2. D — Mix it in planting holes or spread it around crops
   Compost feeds crops and improves the soil.

3. C — In the soil beside the plant
   The bottle is buried neck down near the plant.

4. B — Keeps the soil moist by reducing evaporation
   A covering of dry grass slows down drying of the soil.

5. B — It loses a lot of heat to the air
   Open fires waste heat.

6. D — So the fire does not burn while you are still preparing
   Fuel is not wasted waiting.

7. D — Young shoots of vegetables
   Hares nibble young plants.

8. C — They make noise and flash to frighten animals
   Noise and movement scare animals.

9. C — Water the bed so the soil is soft
   Wet soil lets you pull gently without harming others.

10. B — A young tree joined with a branch from a good tree
   Grafted trees give good quality fruit sooner.

11. B — Carefully so the ball of soil around roots does not break
   Broken roots harm the seedling.

12. B — Share or sell them and avoid wasting
   Extra fruits can earn money or feed others.

13. B — Cover trees with nets or use scare methods
   Peaceful protection.

14. C — To remove germs
   Poultry can carry germs.

15. D — Orange
   Fruits are protective foods.

16. D — Writing what you eat at each meal
   Records help you check your meals.

17. C — Mango
   Mango has vitamins.

18. D — Groundnuts
   Groundnuts give protein and energy.

19. C — Pick one or more foods from each group
   A balanced meal includes all three groups.

20. C — To cool them so they are easy to peel
   Cold water stops cooking and cools the eggs.

21. D — Preparing food using heat
   Cooking uses heat to make food safe and tasty.

22. C — Rubbish or waste
   Refuse means waste.

23. A — Snakes, rats and mosquitoes can hide there
   A tidy compound is safer.

24. C — They may not protect the hands
   Holes let dirt and germs in.

25. C — It helps others learn about PPE and hygiene
   Displays teach and encourage others.

26. B — Measuring
   Measuring gives even and accurate stitches.

27. A — One that shows clearly on the cloth
   It is easy to see and pull out.

28. B — 2 cm
   The long stitch is about 2 cm.

29. C — Long and short tacking
   Long and short tacking is another type.

30. D — About 1 cm each time
   The raw edge is hidden.

SECTION B
----
31. (4 marks)
   Answer: Keep it damp like a squeezed sponge, keep it covered, turn it after two to three weeks, and keep children and animals away.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct care activity, up to 4.

32. (4 marks)
   Answer: Weakness, tiredness, frequent illness, slow growth, poor concentration (any four).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

33. (5 marks)
   Answer: Prepare a fine seedbed; make drills about 1 cm deep; sow seeds thinly with sand; cover and water gently; thin to about 5 cm; weed and water; harvest after three to four months by loosening the soil and pulling.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct stage, up to 5.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: It is dark brown, crumbly, smells like earth, and the original wastes cannot be seen.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sign.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: Even tacking has equal stitches and gaps; long and short tacking has a long stitch followed by a short stitch.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each name and 1 for correct descriptions.

36. (4 marks)
   Answer: Plant fast growing trees on their land for firewood, care for them and replace any tree cut with more new trees, so wood is always available and forests are not cut.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for planting, caring, replacing and result.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: Calf, kid and lamb.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct name.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: Duster from old cloth; mop from strips of cloth on a stick; dustpan from a cut jerrican.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each tool with material.

39. (2 marks)
   Answer: Germs and skin infections spread through them.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for germs, 1 mark for infection.

40. (4 marks)
   Answer: Even tacking is more even and holds more firmly; long and short tacking is quicker because each stitch covers more cloth.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for each stitch description, 1 each for quicker and firmer.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Big trees such as mango grow slowly and need years before flowering, while pawpaw and passion fruit are small plants that fruit within about a year.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for slow trees, fast plants, and reason of size or type.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: A bucket or container, a hose or pipe, and small holes or drippers for water to come out. A stand may also be used.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each item.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: It can carry germs, it may smell or spoil, and clean PPE lasts longer and protects better.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Saves trees and forests, saves money, reduces smoke and illness, saves time looking for firewood.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each benefit.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: Grow vegetables and fruits at home and use cheap proteins such as beans, omena or eggs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
